title: Autonomous syllabus run: no human gates, Fable plans, Sonnet/Opus build
content: Operator ruling 2026-09-04: the remaining supervised-learning curriculum runs as an unattended task list. Fable authors the plan and cards; Sonnet builds practical notebooks and tooling, Opus builds theory notebooks and the final corpus review. No human review gates anywhere in the run: features resolve to the agent tier (config.json review_gates.entity_overrides), verification is mechanical (scripts/verify_notebook.py), agent verdicts are recorded via append-verdict-cli. Operator reads the finished corpus only.

title: File update-task-status-cli column bug upstream
content: Operator ruling 2026-09-04: file, do not hand-fix in the plugin cache. Filed as powell-clark/consciousness#2229 together with the js-yaml resolution defect found while investigating. Until released, the run corrects DONE-index rows via the misplaced-cards healer and records feature verdicts with append-verdict-cli instead of approve/cli.js.

title: Subscription billing, Sonnet-only dispatch, and do not crash the host
content: Operator ruling 2026-09-05, three parts, superseding the model split in STEER-SL005. (1) This is a subscription, not API billing: --max-budget-usd is inert and is removed from every dispatch block; runaway sessions are bounded by --max-turns from the card plus a 90-minute wall-clock cap per task, and total_cost_usd is logged for information only. (2) Every dispatched session is Sonnet; the orchestrator refuses to start if any card names another model. Opus plans and reviews in the operator's own session and dispatches nothing. (3) Do not crash the computer: measured 16 cores, ~6 GB of 31 GB free, disk 85% full, 15-minute load average 10.4 — so the run is strictly sequential with no fan-out, prechecks MemAvailable >= 3 GB and >= 10 GB free disk before each dispatch and each notebook execution, pins OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMEXPR thread counts to 4 of 16, and runs notebook kernels under an address-space rlimit so a runaway allocation raises MemoryError rather than inviting the OOM killer.
